etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English differren, from Old French differer, from Latin differō (“carry apart, put off, defer; differ”), from dis- (“apart”) + ferō (“carry, bear”). Compare Ancient Greek διαφέρω (diaphérō). Doublet of defer (etymology 1).

definitions.definition: (intransitive, people, groups, etc.) To have diverging opinions, disagree.

quote.citation: May 11, 1827, George Canning, Changes in the Administration
quote.text: I differ from the honourable baronet on both these subjects

definitions.definition: (intransitive) Not to have the same traits or characteristics; to be unalike or distinct.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From diff +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: (computing) A program that diffs, a diff.
